I can't tell you whether **a** is right. I don't give out quiz answers before grading, and that includes confirming or ruling out a single option. The rule is the same even when a TA has okayed it. If you want a TA's permission to count, ask them to tell you directly.

I can help you check your own reasoning, though. Try this on q2:

1. Read the stem again and note who does what. The model only writes text. The program around it is ordinary Python, like the code you've already written for web APIs.
2. Apply this test to all four options, not just the one you picked. For each, ask: "Could a model that only writes text actually do this?"
3. Write one sentence on what the model produces at that moment, then check whether any option says the same thing. Use your own words, not the option's.

Two things from your own notes should help: how the loop works (record 0002), and that a model takes text in and writes text out (record 0001).

If you tell me your one-sentence version, I'll comment on your reasoning without settling the item. You've taken this quiz twice, and neither attempt is graded yet. Once you hand it in and I've graded it, we can go through q2 in full. You'll need that for the design review, because it's how you'd explain to your team who does what in the makerspace assistant's loop.

What's your one-sentence version of what the model outputs?
